Source-linked memory for AI.

MESA is open-source memory infrastructure for AI systems. It stores information from your documents and notes, finds what is relevant to a question, and returns it with the source.

QuickstartGitHub

WHY A MEMORY LAYER?

Your assistant needs more than a question.

To answer using your own information, an assistant needs relevant material from your documents. MESA keeps that material retrievable beyond a single conversation, together with the passage and document revision that support it.

WHY NOT PLAIN RAG?

Three differences from a vector database.

01

Answers keep their source

Plain RAG returns text chunks. MESA returns each fact with the document, revision and passage it came from, so your app can show “according to…”.

02

Four ways to find, not one

A vector database only compares meaning. MESA also matches exact words, stored facts and links between things, then merges the rankings.

03

Memory you can correct

Every write is tracked. You can replace a revision, roll back a source or delete a document, and the derived search data follows.

Who it is for
Developers building assistants or agents that must cite their sources — legal research is the first reference use.
Models
Bring your own LLM and embedding provider. See the supported list. Providers →
License
MIT. Runs locally on SQLite, LanceDB and Kùzu — no hosted service.

WHAT CAN YOU BUILD?

Put your information to work.

01

An assistant for your documents

Find relevant passages in a collection of notes or documents, and show which source supports the information.

02

Memory across sessions

Let an agent retrieve previously saved information in later sessions, within its authorized data scope.

03

Work that needs source tracing

Build review workflows where a fact must be traced to a specific document revision and passage.

START WITH THE CORE

Memory is one part of the application.

Core handles memory. Your application supplies source text and uses a language model to turn returned evidence into an answer. Connect over HTTP, from Python, or through MCP (the protocol AI tools use to call external services).

MESA Data → MESA Core → MESA Law

The legal reference path: source preparation → memory → application. Data and Law are separate projects; Core can also serve other applications.
